hints: Notice the two clues from water: a gas is released and the solution becomes alkaline, so think about what type of substance does both.
Recall that Group 2 metals give hydrogen gas plus a hydroxide with water, while metal oxides give only a hydroxide with no gas.
Now compare the hydroxides in sulfuric acid, remembering that barium sulfate is an insoluble white solid while magnesium sulfate stays dissolved.
walkthrough:
**Sort metals from metal oxides using the gas clue**

Think side by side with me. A metal reacting makes hydrogen gas. An oxide dissolving makes no gas.

Metal with water:
$$\text{M} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{M(OH)}_2 + \text{H}_2$$

Oxide with water:
$$\text{MO} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{M(OH)}_2$$

Since a gas is given off, X must be the metal, not the oxide.

**Check the pH clue**

The product $\text{M(OH)}_2$ releases $\text{OH}^-$ ions into solution.

That explains why the pH increases and the solution becomes alkaline. Both barium and magnesium metals could do this in principle.

**Use the sulfuric acid test to pick barium**

Now add dilute sulfuric acid which provides $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ ions.

Barium ions give a classic white precipitate:
$$\text{Ba}^{2+}(aq) + \text{SO}_4^{2-}(aq) \rightarrow \text{BaSO}_4(s)$$

Magnesium sulfate, $\text{MgSO}_4$, is soluble, so no precipitate forms. Only barium fits all three observations.

options.A: Barium reacts vigorously with cold water to give barium hydroxide and hydrogen gas, so pH rises. The resulting $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$ solution then gives insoluble white $\text{BaSO}_4$ with sulfuric acid. It matches all observations.
options.B: Barium oxide does give $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$ and would give white $\text{BaSO}_4$ later, but $\text{BaO} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Ba(OH)}_2$ produces no gas. The gas clue rules it out.
options.C: Magnesium with water would in theory give $\text{Mg(OH)}_2 + \text{H}_2$, but it reacts extremely slowly with cold water and $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ is only sparingly soluble. More importantly, with sulfuric acid it forms soluble $\text{MgSO}_4$, so no white precipitate is seen.
options.D: Magnesium oxide gives $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ with water but with no gas evolved, so it fails the first test. It also fails the second test because magnesium sulfate is soluble and gives no white precipitate.
